title: Why Can Tabs Stay On
coreQuestion: Why does a drink can's tab stay attached after you open it?

facts.claim: In the 1960s, at least one inventor attempted to solve the litter problem by having the tab retained by a stationary key, which was unsuccessful commercially.
Cudzik, an engineer with Reynolds Metals, filed a design patent application for an end closure for a container.
The safety and litter problems were eventually solved later in the 1970s.

narration.text: Why does a can's tab stay attached after you open it?
Early tabs came off, and loose tabs were a litter problem.
In the 1960s, at least one inventor tried to solve it, without commercial success.
The safety and litter problems were solved later in the 1970s.
Daniel Cudzik, an engineer with Reynolds Metals, invented a tab that does not come off.
So the tab stays on the can instead of on the ground.
